review: B02 G1 initial read-only implementation review, authority-boundary follow-up

findings.evidence: The new require_mock_operator_grant trigger rejects any non-mock eligibility INSERT unless current_user owns profile_eligibility, raising SQLSTATE 42501 with fixed message REAL_ELIGIBILITY_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE. The function is not SECURITY DEFINER. The operator grant command and direct operator SQL therefore cannot mint real eligibility; the schema owner can seed synthetic fixtures, and a future approved real issuer requires a new migration.
findings.verdict: The specific B02 G1 boundary is now explicit and matches the plan. Synthetic schema-owner fixtures remain privileged test setup, not evidence of corporate approval.

findings.evidence: migrate.py checks rolreplication and rejects pg_auth_members rows where the configured role is either member or roleid.
operator SELECT is limited to project, authority, profile, job, artifact, and workspace tables; login transactions, sessions, commands, and outbox are excluded.

review_notes.migration: The existing read-only review found one transactional migration with a transaction-scoped advisory lock, schema-owner/role-property checks, per-version source SHA-256 and role pins, drift rejection, and fixed-code CLI errors. DDL and the migration ledger are inside the same transaction.
review_notes.privileges: Runtime job/command/outbox advancement and snapshot mutation remain unavailable. UPDATE(lock_version) on memberships and authorization_guards is narrowly granted for SELECT FOR UPDATE serialization; eligibility reads remain SELECT-only to runtime. Authority changes serialize on the project guard. The PostgreSQL role is an application service role, not per-user project isolation; no RLS claim is made.
review_notes.scope: This remains an initial G1 review, not B02 acceptance. TC-owned real PostgreSQL checks are still required.

verification.performed: Read-only source inspection and SHA-256 pinning of the approved plan and reviewed implementation files.
